m.q: Show the array after each comparison in the FIRST pass of bubble sort on [5,2,8,1,4]. [5 marks]
st: Compare 5 and 8: no swap. Then compare 8 and 1: swap → [2,5,1,8,4].
Compare 8 and 4: swap → [2,5,1,4,8]. Largest value 8 is now at right. [5]

An array is [3,1,2]. Apply a complete pass and explain the result. [4]
3>1 swap → [1,3,2] [2]; 3>2 swap → [1,2,3] [1]; largest element 3 at end [1].

k.q: Predict one adjacent swap of two example file sizes in a bubble-sort pass.
k.code:
leftMB = 7
rightMB = 2
if leftMB > rightMB then
    temp = leftMB
    leftMB = rightMB
    rightMB = temp
endif
print(leftMB)
p: Predict the value printed after the comparison.
Change rightMB to 10 and predict again.
State which values are compared by bubble sort and how to calculate combined file storage.
k.a: 7 > 2 so the values swap; leftMB becomes 2 and is printed. With rightMB 10 there is no swap and 7 prints. Bubble sort compares neighbouring elements. Total file storage requires adding the file sizes, e.g. 7+2=9 MB.
